terms.grammar: adjective, third declension, in the singular
evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.4.13: omnem crēde diem tibi dīlūxisse suprēmum
terms.comment: Every one of a kind, without exception; “not every” is nōn omnis. In the plural it is “all” (see all).

terms.gloss: every (one in a series): every fifth, all the best
terms.grammar: pronoun and adjective, after the superlative or the ordinal it goes with
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.2.139: quīntō quōque annō, every fifth year (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Rab. Post. 34: tertiō quōque verbō, at every other word (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With a superlative, “all the …, every …”: optimus quisque, all the best people; doctissimus quisque, every learned man (Lewis & Short). With an ordinal, every second, third …, counted the Roman way, both ends included: tertiō quōque verbō, “at every other word”. With a word of time, “each”: quōque diē (Cic. Sen. 38). For “each” on its own, see each.

phrases.latin: ut enim nōn omne vīnum, sīc nōn omnis nātūra vetustāte coacēscit
phrases.english: for as not every wine turns sour with age, so not every nature does

phrases.latin: omnem crēde diem tibi dīlūxisse suprēmum; grāta superveniet quae nōn spērābitur hōra
phrases.english: believe that every day that dawns is your last: the hour you did not hope for will come as a welcome gift

phrases.latin: Nōn omnī eundem calceum indūcēs pedī.
phrases.english: You won’t put the same shoe on every foot.

phrases.latin: veterrima quaeque, ut ea vīna quae vetustātem ferunt, esse dēbet suāvissima
phrases.english: every friendship, the older it is, should be the sweeter, like wines that keep

phrases.latin: quid quōque diē dīxerim, audierim, ēgerim, commemorō vesperī
phrases.english: every evening I go over what I said, heard and did that day

sources: Lewis & Short: omnis · Lewis & Short: quisque
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-horatius, loci-publilius), checked against the editions named there.

Publilius is cited as the loci collection numbers him, by position under each initial letter in the Latin Library text; from N onwards that numbering differs from Meyer’s. “Ps.-Publil.” marks lines from the later collections printed with him.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
